must_fix.title: Light-DOM content slotted into a <slot> inside a target is hidden (aria-hidden/inert), both initially and when added later
must_fix.evidence: acceptNode (ariaHideOutside.ts:129-133) only skips flat-tree ancestors of a target, not flat-tree descendants, so light children of a skipped host that are slotted into the target get hidden. Probe (flag on): host

nits: When a target is slotted into a shell's shadow root, whether the shell's other shadow content is hidden depends on whether an unrelated top-layer element lives in that shadow root: test 'does not hide a shadow root that only contains a target through a slot' expects #shadow-sibling visible, while 'keeps the slot wrappers of a slotted target visible when its shadow root is walked for a top layer element' expects #hdr hidden.

report:
I found one bug the contributor needs to fix before this merges: when content is slotted into a target, it gets hidden. The tests, lint and type check all pass. I deleted my probe file and `git status` is back to how I found it (only the four modified files). **Checks run (all pass)** - `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays`: 10 suites, 214 tests passed. - `yarn eslint packages/@react-aria/overlays`: exit 0. - `yarn check-types`: exit 0. - `node scripts/lint-packages.js` and `yarn constraints`: clean. - The new `@react-stately/flags` dependency uses `^3.1.2`, the same as `interactions`, `utils` and `table`. The `yarn.lock` change matches it. - The tests sit next to the existing ones and turn the flag on in a separate `describe` with `beforeAll(enableShadowDOM)`. `FocusScope.test.js` and `usePress.test.js` do the same. **Must fix: content slotted into a target gets hidden** The PR handles a target that is slotted into some other component's shadow root, through `isFlatTreeAncestor` and the slot tests. It does not handle the reverse: light-DOM children of a host that are slotted into a `` *inside* the target. On screen those children are part of the target, but the light-DOM walk reaches them as children of the skipped host. `acceptNode` (`ariaHideOutside.ts:129-133`) only checks whether a node is an ancestor of a target, so it hides them. That contradicts the issue's "everything outside the targets is hidden". `useModalOverlay` and `usePopover` pass `shouldUseInert: true`, so the dialog's own buttons would become inert. I reproduced it with a temporary probe test (flag on): ```js container.innerHTML = ''; sr = host.attachShadow({mode:'open'}); sr.innerHTML = '
'; ariaHideOutside([sr.querySelector('#dialog')]); ``` Output: ``` assignedSlot dialog P1 bg true sib true ok(slotted in dialog) true ``` The same thing happens to content added later. A button appended to the host is slotted into the dialog and still gets hidden: ``` P2 added slotted true true ``` No test covers a target that contains a ``. **Nit** When a target is slotted into a shell's shadow root, whether the shell's other shadow content (such as its header) gets hidden depends on whether an unrelated top-layer element happens to live in that shadow root: - The test "does not hide a shadow root that only contains a target through a slot" expects `#shadow-sibling` to stay visible. - The test "keeps the slot wrappers of a slotted target visible when its shadow root is walked for a top layer element" expects `#hdr` to be hidden. **Edge cases that behaved correctly** - Restoring nested calls: content added after the inner call is reverted is hidden, and everything is restored once the outer call is reverted. - A host added later whose shadow root holds a live announcer: the host and announcer stay visible, its other content is hidden, and content added to that shadow root afterwards is hidden. - The `root` option: shadow content outside it is not hidden. - With the flag off, the code skips every new path. ```json {"mergeable": false, "must_fix": [{"title": "Light-DOM content slotted into a inside a target is hidden (aria-hidden/inert), both initially and when added later", "kind": "bug", "evidence": "acceptNode (ariaHideOutside.ts:129-133) only skips flat-tree ancestors of a target, not flat-tree descendants, so light children of a skipped host that are slotted into the target get hidden. Probe (flag on): host
